title: Adhesion prevention with 4DryField® PH in hysteroscopic surgery
summary:
The purpose of this study is to demonstrate the reduction of postsurgical agglutinations in the uterus by using the medical device 4DryField® PH. If no prophylaxis is performed such agglutinations occur in up to 88% of resections of uterine partition walls, 76% of resections of agglutinations between the uterine walls and 40% of the resections of benign tumors of the uterus. The development of agglutinations in the uterus after operative hysteroscopy can lead to infertility and contribute to miscarriage. Furthermore, agglutinations in the uterus can lead to obliteration of parts of the endometrium cavity, which leads to accumulation of blood in the uterus and strong pain in the lower abdomen. Therefore, the necessity of preventing the formation of agglutinations after a surgical intervention is given.

The test product 4DryField® PH is a medical product consisting of purified, modified starch. It does not contain any components of animal or human origin and is sterile, does not contain ingredients that might induce fever, does not have negative impact on the treated tissue or its metabolism, and has very low allergenic potential. Although the product is routinely used clinically for preventing formation of agglutinations in the uterus, it has not yet been systematically investigated for this indication. If results only roughly as good as those, e.g., after resection of endometriosis, can be achieved, a distinct reduction of linked complications and a clear improvement for the patient can be supposed.

The main objective of this study is to evaluate if the application of 4DryField® PH leads to reduced formation of agglutinations after surgical hysteroscopy. Additionally, it will be investigated if possible consequences of surgery, such as complications, cycle problems, painful menstrual periods, and re-interventions for solving agglutinations can be reduced and the pregnancy rate increased.
conditions: Congenital malformation of uterus and cervix, unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Hysteroscopic surgery for treatment of intrauterine lesions (septa, myoma, adhesions) with second look hysteroscopy
2. Written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnancy and breastfeeding period
2. menopause (FSH>40 mIU/ml, 17β-estradiol<20pg/ml)
3. Malignant tumor of the reproductive organs
4. coagulopathy or a systemic illness that might cause coagulopathy
5. Refusal of follow-up hysteroscopy
6. Expected poor compliance of the patient or patient's inability to understand the purpose of the clinical study
